reader.requirement: At --std 85 [ALL] ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES is the numeric value 0 when associated with a numeric or numeric-edited item (MOVE, compare, arithmetic, VALUE) and one or more '0' characters otherwise, sized to the associated item (GRL2.1) or one character when unassociated (GRL2.2); the word ALL is redundant (SRL3.3), so ALL ZERO is also admitted where a numeric literal is required (SRL3.1); ZERO is refused to an alphabetic receiver (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 b).

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: ALL ZERO where a numeric literal is required is legal at 85 (ALL redundant, §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 SRL3.3) and refused from 2002 (COBOL0902); the ZERO value and fill are one path

reader.notes: ZERO binds to BoundFigurative('Z') whose fill is '0' in every context; numeric receivers take the numeric value through the MOVE/arithmetic paths. PERFORM ZERO TIMES is refused, which agrees with 1985: integer-1 is not 'literal' in the format and the 1985 definition of integer is a numeric literal. S4/C4 DISPLAY shows a leading +, a DISPLAY rendering matter outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: Attack on ZERO against numeric-edited items, which the reader's requirement folds into 'numeric value 0' but 1985 compares as nonnumeric (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.1 applies only to class numeric). src/z_edit.cob at 85: MOVE ZERO TO ZZ9.99 -> '  0.00', IF E5 = ZERO NE; 999.99 '000.00' = ZERO NE; ZZZ '   ' = ZERO NE both orders; PIC 999 BLANK WHEN ZERO -> spaces; 9PP and PP9 VALUE ZERO = ZERO EQ. All agree with ZERO as '0' characters in a nonnumeric comparison and numeric value 0 in a MOVE (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3). src/z_value.cob: VALUE ZERO on ZZ9.99 -> '000000', on XBX -> '000', group VALUE ZERO -> '0000': unedited initialization as §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b requires ('have no effect on initialization of the data item'). Reader's z4 covers the 85-only ALL ZERO arm. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 GR1; OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.1 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value'; OK §1985:VI.5.15.4.
